source.rationale: New gap category, distinct from the single-section multi-SPAN gap (001/006/024/025): here ONE code change is documented in TWO separate, non-adjacent doc SECTIONS (a Quickstart example early in the doc, and a later Reference/Parameters section) that are not ancestor/descendant of each other, so Entry 17's ancestor-dedup logic should NOT collapse them -- both should link independently. Tests whether the pipeline finds and processes both sections, and whether the Corrector's per-finding (not per-doc) design naturally handles this by producing two separate findings, or whether something merges/drops one.

## Reference

### Parameters

* `path` -- directory to snapshot.

Each call to `snapshot()` always produces a full, standalone copy.

labels.notes_for_labeler: CONFIRMED (real run) for the 'Reference' section only (the one recorded as stale_doc_section) -- clean, accurate proposed/approved fix. HARNESS GAP EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED, not just theorized: the run never touched the Quickstart section at all (recorded under the non-standard stale_doc_section_quickstart key, which run_eval.py simply ignores) -- so the actual multi-section-linking hypothesis this case exists to test is still completely untested. Needs either a run_eval.py extension to accept multiple doc sections per case, or a full main.py run against a real repo where both sections genuinely exist and get independently linked.
